title: Does the sum change if we circle different numbers?
description: The circle and strike game is played afresh on the same grid, with different numbers each time. Two new plays are added one at a time and both give the same total as the book's first play.
teaching_notes: One idea: different circles in the same grid can give the same total, so test with a few plays before guessing. Watch for students who expect the sum to change just because the circled numbers are different.

video_script.why: The child plays the game afresh on the same grid with different numbers and compares the sums.
video_script.substitution: The book's own grid, with two new plays of four numbers each.
video_script.anchor: a four by four grid of plus and minus numbers from the book
video_script.payoff_line: Different circles gave different numbers, but the sum was the same, negative one, every time.

final_answer.value: The sum is the same (-1) every time
final_answer.spoken: the sum is the same, negative one, every time

hold_back: The sum is the same (-1) every time
maths_rules: game: circle one number in each row and each column, so no two circled numbers share a row or a column
new play one: 4 (row 1, column 2), -2 (row 2, column 1), 7 (row 3, column 4), -10 (row 4, column 3); 4 + (-2) = 2, 2 + 7 = 9, 9 + (-10) = -1
new play two: 0 (row 1, column 3), -2 (row 2, column 1), 2 (row 3, column 2), -1 (row 4, column 4); 0 + (-2) = -2, -2 + 2 = 0, 0 + (-1) = -1
the book's first play, -1, 9, -7, -2, also makes -1
a plus number moves up the number line and a minus number moves down
video_script.design: The same grid shown three times, once for each play. The circled numbers are added one at a time on an upright number line, teal for moving up and amber for moving down.
